name: ABetaA21G Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Identification of the ABetaA21G mutation in the amyloid precursor protein gene
Demonstration of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence in tissue biopsy
Presence of characteristic clinical manifestations such as progressive sensorimotor neuropathy and cardiac involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of ABetaA21G mutation plus histological evidence of amyloid deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other amyloidosis types and correlation with clinical presentation

searchTerms: progressive nerve damage affecting movement and sensation
loss of feeling and strength in limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposition in cardiac tissue causing restrictive cardiomyopathy
Congo red-positive amyloid deposits with apple-green birefringence on biopsy
searchTerms: diagnostic biopsy with Congo red stain

common.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic neuropathy
searchTerms: dizziness on standing from nerve damage

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal dysmotility including diarrhea and constipation
searchTerms: diarrhea and constipation from gut nerve issues

common.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: carpal tunnel caused by amyloid infiltration

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema secondary to cardiac dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Nephrotic syndrome due to renal amyloid deposits
searchTerms: protein in urine from amyloid buildup

occasional.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome-related thenar muscle atrophy
searchTerms: thumb muscle wasting from nerve compression

rare.symptomName: Vitreous opacities from ocular amyloid deposits
Cutaneous purpura due to vascular amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: purple skin spots from blood vessel damage
skin bruising due to vessel infiltration

laboratory: Abnormal serum and urine protein electrophoresis usually negative for monoclonal proteins
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing late gadolinium enhancement consistent with amyloid infiltration
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating sensorimotor polyneuropathy
other: Tissue biopsy with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence under polarized light

distinguishingFeatures: TTR gene mutations instead of APP gene
Predominant neuropathy with less frequent cardiac restrictive phenotype
Different amyloid fibril protein on biopsy
Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
Rapidly progressive cardiac and renal involvement
Response to chemotherapy targeting plasma cells

redFlags: Rapidly progressive peripheral neuropathy with autonomic dysfunction
Restrictive cardiomyopathy with preserved ejection fraction
Positive Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence on biopsy
references: Glenner GG, et al. Amyloid fibril protein in familial amyloidosis. J Clin Invest. 1989.
Merlini G, Bellotti V. Molecular mechanisms of amyloidosis. N Engl J Med. 2003.
